findings.detail:
trust.toml pins a peer that no acl.toml row with auth_path "pin" matches — neither its device:<name> principal nor its fp:sha256:<fingerprint> principal. Every request from this peer is denied (default-deny) until a matching row exists. (peer: laptop)
minimal example:
[[acl]]
principal = "device:laptop"
allow = ["exec.run", "session.open", "session.list", "session.attach", "session.control"]
findings.remedy: Add a matching [[acl]] row (ADR-0017), then restart serve/listen — acl.toml is only read once at process start.

findings.detail: trust.toml has at least one pinned peer. Removing a pin or lowering its role closes that peer's established connections. It applies to new connections from the next handshake, and to connections held open by a running `qsh serve`, `qsh listen` or `qsh serve --to` within 2 seconds. It applies on this device only; no other device is told. It does not end sessions: a session on a closed connection is detached, and a peer that is still trusted can reconnect and resume it.
findings.remedy: Trust is withdrawn per device: run the same `qsh trust remove` (or `qsh trust set-role`) on every other device that trusts the peer. To end the peer's sessions as well, close them with `qsh session close`.

findings.detail: No platform service unit is registered for this machine's inferred run mode. Until one is, this mode only runs in the foreground; it does not survive logout, reboot, or a crash. (inferred mode: serve)
findings.remedy: Run `qsh service install` to write this mode's unit and start it. docs/deploy/service.md has the same steps by hand: `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID …` (macOS) or `systemctl --user enable --now …` (Linux).
